chunks: Ali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad al-Kunasi, who said: It was narrated to us with an unbroken chain going up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding His Statement, Mighty is His Mention: 'And whoever is careful of (his duty to) Allah, He will make for him an outlet And He provides for him from (sources) he never could imagine'.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'These are a people from our Shites who are weak, who do not have the means to carry (the burden of learning) to us, so they hear our Hadith and accumulate from our knowledge.'
A people who are higher than them, who spend their wealth, tiring their bodies, until they come to us, hear our Hadith, and transmit it to them. So these ones preserve it, whilst those ones waste it.
So they are the ones for whom Allah, Mighty is His Mention, Makes an outlet for them and Gives them Sustenance from a source which they had not even considered beforehand.
And regarding the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Has not there come to you the news of the overwhelming calamity?' He said: 'These are the ones who have cheated the Imam'.
Up to the Statement of the Mighty and Majestic: 'Which will neither nourish nor satisfy hunger'.

He said: 'It will neither benefit them, nor free them from needs. It will not benefit them with the entering (marital relationships), nor free them from the need of sitting down (from begging for more)'.
ai.seo_question: How does the Imam interpret the Quranic verse about Allah making an outlet for those who are careful of Him?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates Surah At-Talaq (65:3) by highlighting the divine provision for the 'weak' Shi'a who, despite lacking resources, benefit from the scholarly efforts of the wealthy who travel to transmit hadith. This interpretation underscores the communal responsibility of knowledge transmission, where the financial sacrifice of the wealthy serves as a means of sustenance for the intellectually eager but resource-poor. Additionally, he connects the 'Ghashiyah' (Overwhelming Calamity) to those who seek proximity to the Imam for status, noting that their presence neither nourishes their souls nor satisfies their spiritual hunger.
